A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same WeightLoRA research work, with readable main text, Figures 1–3, Tables 1–9, and Appendices A–B. Textual and visual inspection supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning results on GLUE, SQuAD, XSum, and CNN/DailyMail, together with adapter-selection and GPU-memory experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–5 and random-adapter ablation in Table 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 retain the same trainable adapter weights, StoIHT/top-K selection, pruning procedure, and WeightLoRA+ rank expansion. The initialization options are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GLUE tasks, SQuAD v1.1/v2.0, XSum, and CNN/DailyMail datasets. No evaluated task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains full fine-tuning, LoRA, AdaLoRA, IncreLoRA, Dynamic LoRA, LoRA-drop, ALoRA, MELoRA, and FlexLoRA. Comparator membership in Tables 2–6 is also unchanged, including RLoRA in the ablation.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same reported model configurations, adapter placements and ranks, metrics, tuning grids, training budgets, batch sizes, and gradient accumulation settings.

E4.justification: The adapter-gradient analysis in Figure 2, GPU-memory sweep in Figure 3, and learned-versus-random adapter selection at K = 1, 5, and 10 in Table 6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B states in both versions that results are averaged across five random seeds. Repeated-run disclosures and statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain the same numerical entries, and Figures 2–3 retain the same plotted findings. For example, Table 3's average for WeightLoRA+ at rank 8 remains 0.9258.

T1.justification: The Taylor-expansion argument, sparsity-constrained formulation, rank-extension mathematics, and Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same definitions and notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive adapter selection, reduced trainable parameters, and WeightLoRA+ performance. Text moving across page breaks does not change these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of adapter importance, memory-versus-accuracy tradeoffs, and learned selection outperforming random selection are retained. Discussions of hyperparameter tuning and computational constraints are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical software, hardware, optimizer, hyperparameter, and training-schedule information, including Tables 7–9. The conclusion provides the same source-code link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, and positioning of trainable adapter weights relative to previous methods are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: The affiliation block changes from the earlier MIPT/ISP RAS/Sber AI Lab entries to Moscow Center for Advanced Studies/SB AI Lab, with corresponding author superscript updates and Innopolis retained. Scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Four institutional logos are removed from the title-page banner, and affiliations are compacted into one line. The shorter header causes text reflow and shifts some figure/table placements, while scientific graphics, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliations and title-page presentation while retaining the methods, claims, experiments, results, and appendix details. These limited presentation edits establish no meaningful net improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
